title: Sourdough Starter
notes: Sourdough starter is a natural yeast that you can make easily at home. It requires a few days growing time, but if looked after can then it can be kept for many years, even generations. This is a very basic primer, do some more reading on how to use and look after your starter longterm. Any time you use the starter make sure you reserve at least a half a cup in the original container and continue feeding so you will not have to start over.

methodSections.heading: To Start a Starter
steps: Mix the flour and water to form a paste and transfer it into a clean jar or bowl with at least a 1.5 litre volume. Cover the container but the lid cannot be airtight, there must be a flow of air but also no fruit flies. Using a paper coffee filter and rubberband is one option. Keep the container in a warm place, a window sill perhaps, for 24 hours.

The flour water mixture will act as a medium to attract natural yeasts and microorganisms to grow. Every 24 hours you need to feed the starter with ¼ Cup unbleached flour and ¼ Cup water, mixing it in thoroughly.

After 3-4 days, you should notice the starter is becoming bubbly and looking alive. This is a good sign! Keep feeding it for another day or so, until you really notice some vigorous bubble action. Then it is ready to use.
